title: National food safety supervisor and training requirements (Standard 3.2.2A)
summary: From 8 December 2023 food service, catering and some retail businesses everywhere in Australia must have a certified food safety supervisor and trained food handlers, and higher-risk businesses must keep records. Before this, whether a supervisor was required depended on the state.

instruments.title: Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code – Standard 3.2.2A – Food Safety Management Tools
instruments.provisions: food safety supervisor, food handler training and record keeping

direction_rationale: The Productivity Commission's 2009 benchmarking found that the most significant difference between states' food safety rules was the requirement for a food safety supervisor; the standard makes it national but adds requirements where none applied.

industries.name: Cafes, Restaurants and Takeaway Food Services

verified.notes: Making date from the Federal Register; the December 2023 start is from FSANZ's page on the standard ('requirements that came in December 2023'); 8 December from the date the consequential variation took effect on the Federal Register.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 29 October 2026 (tranche 3: laws in regulatory regimes with no register items) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: One national requirement replaces state-by-state rules on food safety supervisors, but adds training, supervisor and record-keeping costs for businesses in states that did not require them.

marks.reason: Food businesses in several states meet one requirement instead of different state rules.
Adds supervisor certification, training and records where they were not required before.

assessment.confidence_note: No estimate of the net cost was found; the health benefits of safer food are not weighed here.

responsible.note: FSANZ develops the standard; state and territory food regulators and councils enforce it.
